slides.say: Given: x is a prime number, and x to the power of six is a two-digit number. What is nine x?

So x is a prime, and its sixth power has only two digits. That's a big hint, because a sixth power grows really fast, so x must be a small number. And look, they don't ask for x, they ask for nine x. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, trial and error first, and then plugging in the answers.

[short pause] Our first method, trial and error. Remember, with primes we can simply try numbers against the conditions. Which prime do I try? Look at the choices. Nine times two is eighteen, and eighteen is right there. So the real question is, could a bigger prime work too? Let's try the next prime, three.
I don't write out three times three times three, six times. I build it from what I know. Three to the power of three is twenty-seven. Times three again, that's three to the power of four, eighty-one.
And one more three? Eighty-one times three is already past two digits, and we still need one more three after that. So I don't even need the exact number. Three is too big.
And what does that mean? A bigger base gives a bigger power. So five, seven and every bigger prime are too big too. So x is smaller than three, and the only prime smaller than three is two.
Do I need to calculate two to the power of six? No. The question tells us there is such an x, and two is the only prime left. So x is two.

Now careful, because x isn't the answer. A lot of students find that x is two, and go looking for two in the choices. They ask for nine x. Nine times two is eighteen, so choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Our second method, plugging in the answers. Each choice is nine x, so to get x back, I divide the choice by nine. Twenty-seven over nine is three, eighteen over nine is two, sixty-three over nine is seven, and forty-five over nine is five.
Are they primes? Three, two, seven and five, yes, all four. So the prime condition doesn't rule anything out here, and the power has to decide.
Choice number one gives x is three. Three to the power of three is twenty-seven, and times three is eighty-one. One more three already passes two digits, so choice number one is out.
at: Three to the power of three

slides.say: Choice numbers three and four give seven and five. They're bigger than three, so their powers are even bigger. Both out.
Three choices are out, and choice number two, x is two, is the only one left. So choice number two is our answer.
at: So choice number two is our answer

slides.say: So once a power passes the limit, stop calculating, it's out. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
